one_liner: Research GEMM variant (UNICAMP, OpenBLAS-derived kernels) that skips repacking between chained GEMMs; about 2.25x over OpenBLAS on chains.
what_it_does: LP-GEMM speeds up sequences of dependent GEMMs, as in transformer attention/MLP blocks or consecutive conv layers, by keeping intermediate results in the packed, tiled layout instead of converting back to row/column-major after each call. It splits GEMM into three kernels: ini-GEMM packs the inputs and emits the propagated layout, mid-GEMM consumes and emits that layout, and end-GEMM unpacks to the canonical BLAS layout. The authors say it is not BLAS-API compliant: callers must thread layout metadata through the chain and adapt any ops in between (softmax, RoPE, RMSNorm).
how_it_is_fast: The technique is layout propagation, i.e. packing elimination across operator boundaries. The micro-kernel writes C in the same tiled order the next GEMM's packed operand expects, so the O(n^2) pack and unpack steps around each O(n^3) micro-kernel run only at the ends of the chain. The kernels are derived from OpenBLAS (AVX-512 with mr=16, nr=4 on x86; RVV 1.0 with mr=16, nr=8 on RISC-V), so per-kernel FLOP efficiency is about OpenBLAS's level and the gain comes from the data movement it removes.
when_to_use: Chains of small to medium GEMMs where packing is a large share of runtime, e.g. LLM attention at short sequence lengths (the paper shows about 2x at 10 tokens on x86)
Edge or CPU inference engines you control end to end, so custom layouts can flow between ops
RISC-V RVV 1.0 targets where OpenBLAS's unpack step is slow
As a design reference for fusing packing across operators in your own GEMM or ML compiler
when_not_to_use: As a library: no LP-GEMM kernels are public (the linked simple_attention repo is a naive-matmul Llama driver that links a libopenblas not included in the repo)
Single, isolated GEMM calls: the initial kernel performs about like OpenBLAS, and BLIS and FlashGEMM median speedups beat it there
Large matrices (for example the MLP at about 1.1x on x86), where packing is negligible
beta != 0 accumulation into existing C, which needs explicit packing
Multi-threaded workloads: only single-threaded results are reported

integration.form: not released (paper only; authors give a contact email)
integration.min_toolchain: not documented (driver Makefile uses g++ -mavx512f -fopenmp with no -O flag)
integration.platforms: x86-64 AVX-512 (Xeon Gold 6252), RISC-V RV64GCV with RVV 1.0 (SpacemiT K1 X60)

gotchas: Results stay in the propagated tiled layout, so every non-GEMM op between GEMMs (softmax, RoPE, RMSNorm) needs a layout-aware rewrite; softmax pays extra at tile boundaries

The 'up to 5x for RISC-V' claim (Section V-C) is a speedup that rises with token count to 500 tokens and is attributed to a weak OpenBLAS RVV unpack kernel, not to LP-GEMM itself; the verifier found Fig. 6b peaks at about 1.5x, inconsistent with that text
Compiler, flags and OpenBLAS/BLIS/MKL versions are not stated
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Siblings such as BLASFEO, LibShalom and IAAT speed up individual small GEMMs; LP-GEMM's idea only pays off across chains of dependent GEMMs, and with no code it is a technique to copy, not a library to adopt. For a usable single-call kernel choose BLASFEO or LibShalom.
verified_claims_summary: Single-threaded on an Intel Xeon Gold 6252 (AVX-512), chained GEMMs averaged 2.25x over OpenBLAS; mid/end kernels had a median of about 1.5x on single GEMMs from GEMMBench, and MKL and oneDNN stayed close. RISC-V (SpacemiT X60, RVV 1.0) attention results vs OpenBLAS are reported, but the abstract-level 5x does not match Fig. 6b per the verifier; compiler and flags are not given.
status_note: arXiv 2604.04599 preprint (2026, no venue stated) with no released kernels and no license, so it is listed as a reference only.
